entry.description: In 0.7.0 SparkGenerator rejects pk/fk ('NumPy engine only in 0.7.0'). Design: port the key function to native Spark expressions over spark.range(size) — F.xxhash64(F.lit(col_seed).cast('long'), F.col('id')) matches the NumPy xxh64_long bit for bit (prototype spark_parity.py, 50k rows); F.pmod for the parent index; sequence and affine permutation are plain arithmetic; Feistel as a native round loop or mapInPandas over the NumPy core. No Python UDF; never F.rand(seed), whose output changes with the partition count. Parity test: same spec and seed on both engines give identical pk/fk columns. The NumPy core stays the reference; a pure addition, since 0.7.0 keys are hash- and index-based.

entry.description: The old watermark's intent, rebuilt statelessly (load-realism phase). Design: event time is a function of the row index (born(i) = start + i/rate) for parent and child; an fk kwarg born_before limits the child's parent index range to parents born at or before the child's event time — alive(j) = number of parent indices with born(p) <= t(j), p = sampler(hash(seed, j)) mod alive(j), skew applied over permuted ranks as in 0.7.0. No clock, no database; parent and child producers need no coordination across processes. Market study prototype: no child before its parent, identical output for 1 or N chunks.
